sorular.soru: What does the word "tajweed" mean in Arabic?
sorular.aciklama: In Arabic, "tajweed" means "to beautify, to make beautiful." This discipline teaches how to recite the letters of the Quran correctly and beautifully.

sorular.soru: In which surah is the verse "Recite the Quran with measured recitation" found?
sorular.aciklama: The verse "Recite the Quran with measured recitation" is found in al-Muzzammil 73:4. Measured recitation means reading the Quran slowly, distinctly, and thoughtfully.

sorular.soru: In which surah is the verse "We have recited it in measured recitation" found?
sorular.aciklama: The expression "We have recited it in measured recitation" appears in al-Furqan 25:32. This verse indicates that the Quran was revealed with measured recitation.

sorular.soru: What is the basic responsibility regarding the correct recitation of enough of the Quran to perform salah?
secenekler: A) It is an individual responsibility to pronounce the letters correctly enough to avoid changing the meaning
C) It is obligatory only for those who have memorized the Quran
D) It is enough simply to recite in a beautiful voice
sorular.aciklama: In salah, al-Fatihah and the surahs in particular must be recited without changing the letters and while avoiding obvious errors that would alter the meaning. Learning the details of tajweed is a process that develops step by step.

sorular.soru: How many points of articulation are there in total in Quranic tajweed?
sorular.aciklama: The places from which letters are pronounced are called points of articulation. In the classical account, there are 17 points of articulation, grouped in the throat, tongue, lips, and nasal passage.

sorular.soru: How many letters are always pronounced with a heavy sound (the elevated letters)?
sorular.aciklama: There are 7 letters that are always pronounced with a heavy sound: خ ص ض ط ظ غ ق

sorular.soru: When is the letter Ra (ر) pronounced with a light sound?
secenekler: A) When it has a kasrah
B) When it has a fathah
C) When it has a dammah
D) It is always pronounced with a light sound
sorular.aciklama: Ra is pronounced with a heavy sound when it has a fathah or dammah, and with a light sound when it has a kasrah. When it has a sukun, the preceding vowel is considered.

sorular.soru: What does "tafkheem" mean?
secenekler: A) Pronouncing with a light sound
C) Pronouncing with a heavy sound
sorular.aciklama: Tafkheem is pronouncing letters with a heavy, full sound. Its opposite is tarqeeq, or pronouncing with a light sound.

sorular.soru: What does "tarqeeq" mean?
secenekler: A) Pronouncing with a heavy sound
B) Pronouncing with a light sound
C) Pronouncing with a concealed sound
sorular.aciklama: Tarqeeq is pronouncing letters with a light, thin sound. The letters خ ص ض ط ظ غ ق are always considered heavy; some other letters have special cases.

sorular.soru: From which point of articulation are the letters Mim (م) and Ba (ب) pronounced?
secenekler: C) The tip of the tongue
sorular.aciklama: Ba (ب) and Mim (م) are pronounced by closing both lips completely. Therefore, when Ba follows a sakin Mim, lip ikhfa is applied; they are close to each other because they share the same point of articulation.

sorular.soru: Which are the qalqalah letters?
secenekler: A) ق ط ب ج د
B) ء ه ع ح غ خ
D) ت ث ج د ذ
sorular.aciklama: There are 5 qalqalah letters: ق ط ب ج د — they can be memorized as "Kutbe Cd".

sorular.soru: What condition must a letter be in for qalqalah to be applied?
secenekler: A) It must have a shaddah
B) It must have a vowel mark
C) It must have a sukun (no vowel)
D) It must have a fathah
sorular.aciklama: When qalqalah letters have a sukun, or when stopping at the end of a word, they are pronounced with a slight echo. If one stops on a qalqalah letter with a shaddah, the qalqalah is heard more distinctly.

sorular.soru: In which two letters is ghunnah found?
sorular.aciklama: Ghunnah, a resonant sound from the nasal passage, is found only in the letters Mim (م) and Nun (ن).

sorular.soru: How long is ghunnah held?
secenekler: A) The length of one vowel count
B) The length of three vowel counts
C) The length of four alifs
D) The length of two vowel counts
sorular.aciklama: Ghunnah lasts for the time it takes to pronounce two vowel counts.

sorular.soru: What is a practical way to tell whether ghunnah is being performed correctly?
secenekler: A) Pinch the nose while reciting — if the sound changes, the ghunnah is correct
C) Touch the tip of the tongue to the palate
D) Produce the sound from the throat
sorular.aciklama: If the sound changes when you pinch your nose while reciting ghunnah, the ghunnah is being performed correctly; if the sound stays the same, the nasal passage is not being used.

sorular.soru: What is tanween?
secenekler: A) A Nun without a vowel mark
B) A Mim with a shaddah
C) A double vowel mark at the end of a word
sorular.aciklama: Tanween consists of double vowel marks at the end of a word that produce an n sound: ً ٍ ٌ. A sakin Nun, on the other hand, is a Nun without a vowel mark or with a sukun.

sorular.soru: How many different rules are applied after tanween and sakin Nun?
sorular.aciklama: Depending on the letter that follows tanween or sakin Nun, 4 different rules are applied: izhar, idgham, iqlab, and ikhfa.

sorular.soru: What is the Turkish meaning of the word "izhar"?
sorular.aciklama: Izhar means "to pronounce clearly and distinctly." When a throat letter follows tanween or sakin Nun, the Nun sound is pronounced clearly.

sorular.soru: How many izhar letters are there?
sorular.aciklama: There are 6 izhar letters: ء ه ع ح غ خ — all are throat letters.

sorular.soru: What is done if the letter "غ" (ghayn) follows a sakin Nun?
sorular.aciklama: "غ" (ghayn) is an izhar letter (the throat letters are: ء ه ع ح غ خ). Therefore, the sakin Nun is pronounced clearly.

sorular.soru: What does "idgham" mean?
secenekler: B) Pronouncing one letter by merging it into another
C) Pronouncing a letter with concealment
D) Pronouncing a letter by transforming it
sorular.aciklama: Idgham is when the Nun sound shifts into a particular letter that follows tanween or sakin Nun.

sorular.soru: What does the mnemonic word "Yemenu" help us remember?
secenekler: D) The letters of idgham with ghunnah
sorular.aciklama: "Yemenu" (ي م ن و) helps us remember the 4 letters with which idgham is performed with ghunnah: Ya, Mim, Nun, and Waw.

sorular.soru: With which two letters is idgham performed without ghunnah?
sorular.aciklama: The letters Lam (ل) and Ra (ر) are the letters of idgham without ghunnah. The Nun sound is silently merged into these letters.

sorular.soru: What is done if sakin Nun and Ya occur together in the same word?
secenekler: A) Idgham is performed with ghunnah
B) Idgham is performed without ghunnah
sorular.aciklama: If sakin Nun and an idgham letter occur together within the same word, idgham is not performed; izhar is applied. Idgham is applied only between two separate words.

sorular.soru: What does the word "iqlab" mean?
sorular.aciklama: Iqlab means "to transform." When Ba follows tanween or sakin Nun, the Nun sound changes into a Mim sound.

sorular.soru: In iqlab, into which sound does the Nun sound change?
secenekler: B) A Nun sound pronounced heavily
sorular.aciklama: In iqlab, nun sakinah or tanwin changes into a mim sound and is recited with ghunnah. A small م appears at this point in the mushaf.

sorular.soru: How many letters is ikhfa applied with?
sorular.aciklama: There are 15 ikhfa letters: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك

sorular.soru: How is the nun sound recited in ikhfa?
secenekler: B) By changing completely into a mim sound
C) Concealed with a slight nasal resonance
sorular.aciklama: In ikhfa, the nun sound is not pronounced fully; it is concealed with a slight nasal resonance (ghunnah). It is not as clear as in izhar or as complete as in idgham.

sorular.soru: Which mark appears in the mushaf where iqlab occurs?
sorular.aciklama: A small م (mim) is written in the mushaf where iqlab occurs; it shows that the nun sound has changed into a mim sound.

sorular.soru: How many rules are there for mim sakinah?
sorular.aciklama: There are 3 rules for mim sakinah: Idgham al-Mithlayn, Ikhfa Shafawi, and Izhar Shafawi.

sorular.soru: What is done if a vowelled mim follows mim sakinah?
secenekler: A) Idgham al-Mithlayn — they merge with ghunnah
sorular.aciklama: If a vowelled mim follows mim sakinah, the two mims merge (Idgham al-Mithlayn) and are recited with ghunnah.

sorular.soru: When is "Ikhfa Shafawi" (labial ikhfa) applied?
secenekler: A) When mim follows mim sakinah
B) When nun follows mim sakinah
C) When ba follows mim sakinah
D) When ha follows mim sakinah
sorular.aciklama: If ba (ب) follows mim sakinah, Ikhfa Shafawi (labial ikhfa) is applied: it is recited in a concealed manner with ghunnah, without closing the lips.

sorular.soru: When is "Izhar Shafawi" (labial izhar) applied?
secenekler: A) When ba follows mim sakinah
B) When a letter other than mim or ba follows mim sakinah
C) When nun follows mim sakinah
D) When hamzah follows mim sakinah
sorular.aciklama: When any letter other than mim or ba follows mim sakinah, Izhar Shafawi (labial izhar) is applied; the mim is pronounced clearly.

sorular.soru: Why is mim recited without closing the lips in Ikhfa Shafawi?
secenekler: A) Because ba is a throat letter
B) Because mim is a heavy letter
C) Because the mim sound must be completely swallowed
D) Because ba and mim have the same articulation point; when the lips close, the transition is made in a concealed manner with ghunnah
sorular.aciklama: Ba and mim share the same articulation point (the lips). When ba follows mim sakinah, the transition is made with ghunnah without closing the lips—this both conceals the mim and allows a natural transition to ba.

sorular.soru: What are the madd letters?
sorular.aciklama: There are three madd letters: alif (ا), waw (و), and ya (ي). Alif is a basic elongation letter when the preceding letter has a fathah, waw when the preceding letter has a dammah, and ya when the preceding letter has a kasrah.

sorular.soru: How long is the elongation in Madd Tabii?
sorular.aciklama: Madd Tabii (natural, basic elongation) is elongated for the length of 1 alif. In this rule, the madd letter is not followed by a hamzah or a sukun/jazm.

sorular.soru: When does Madd Muttasil occur?
secenekler: A) When a hamzah follows a madd letter in a different word
B) When a hamzah follows a madd letter in the same word
C) When a sukun follows a madd letter
D) When a letter with a shaddah follows a madd letter
sorular.aciklama: Madd Muttasil (joined madd) occurs when a hamzah follows a madd letter in the same word. The hamzah being in the same word is the distinguishing feature of this rule.

sorular.soru: For how many alifs is Madd Muttasil elongated?
sorular.aciklama: In the commonly taught Hafs recitation, Madd Muttasil is generally elongated for 4 alifs.

sorular.soru: What is the main difference between Madd Munfasil and Madd Muttasil?
secenekler: A) In Muttasil, the hamzah is in the same word; in Munfasil, it is in a separate word
B) Muttasil is elongated for a shorter time
C) In Munfasil, the hamzah is in the same word
D) They are the same rule with different names
sorular.aciklama: In Muttasil, the madd letter and hamzah are in the same word. In Munfasil, the madd letter is in one word and the hamzah is in a separate word; the length of elongation may vary according to the recitation tradition.

sorular.soru: When does Madd Lazim occur?
secenekler: B) When a hamzah occurs in the same word
C) When a letter with a shaddah or jazm follows a madd letter
D) When a letter with a fathah precedes waw or ya
sorular.aciklama: Madd Lazim (obligatory madd) occurs when an original sukun/jazm or a shaddah follows a madd letter in the same word. In common teaching, it is elongated for 4 alifs.

sorular.soru: When does Madd Arid occur?
secenekler: A) When a hamzah follows a madd letter
B) When a syllable normally read short is elongated when stopping (waqf)
C) When a letter with a shaddah follows a madd letter
D) When the letter ba follows a madd letter
sorular.aciklama: Madd Arid (temporary madd) occurs at a place where the reciter stops. Waqf means stopping while reciting in a way that preserves the meaning.

sorular.soru: What two basic conditions are required for Madd Lin?
secenekler: A) A hamzah and sukun must follow a madd letter
B) An elongation letter must occur before a letter with a shaddah
C) One must stop at a word containing a hamzah
D) Waw or ya must have a jazm, and the preceding letter must have a fathah
sorular.aciklama: For Madd Lin, waw (و) or ya (ي) must have a jazm/be sakin, and the preceding letter must have a fathah. This madd becomes particularly apparent at waqf. Example: خَوْف (havf).

sorular.soru: In Shamsiyyah, how is the lam after the prefix "el" pronounced?
secenekler: A) It is swallowed, and the following letter is pronounced with a shaddah
C) It is pronounced with ghunnah
sorular.aciklama: In Shamsiyyah, the lam is assimilated and the following letter is pronounced with a shaddah. Example: "ash-shams"—there is no lam.

sorular.soru: Which rule does the alif-lam in the word "el-kamer" (moon) illustrate?
sorular.aciklama: In the word "el-kamer", the lam is pronounced clearly; qaf is a qamariyyah letter. Qamariyyah brings to mind the moon letters with which the lam sound is heard.

sorular.soru: What does the م (mim) waqf mark in the mushaf mean?
secenekler: A) One may stop or continue
B) One must stop here; continuing may cause confusion in the meaning
C) It is preferable to continue
sorular.aciklama: At the م (Waqf Lazim) mark, one must stop; continuing may distort or confuse the meaning. This mark guides the reader in preserving the meaning.

sorular.soru: What does the لا (la) waqf mark in the mushaf mean?
secenekler: B) It is preferable to stop
C) One may either stop or continue
D) One should not stop and should continue
sorular.aciklama: The لا (Waqf Mamnu) mark generally means that one should not stop and should continue. If one has to stop, one resumes from an appropriate place that completes the meaning.

sorular.soru: What is Lahn-i Jali?
secenekler: A) A major error in pronouncing a letter or word that can affect the meaning
B) A minor error such as insufficient ikhfa or ghunnah
D) Not observing the stopping signs
sorular.aciklama: Lahn-i Jali (an obvious or major error) is the clearly incorrect pronunciation of a letter or word. Major errors that change the meaning may affect the validity of salah.

sorular.soru: How does Lahn-i Khafi affect salah?
secenekler: A) It invalidates salah in every case
B) It invalidates salah and requires it to be made up
C) It generally does not invalidate salah; it reduces the perfection of the recitation
D) It has no significance in tajweed
sorular.aciklama: Lahn-i Khafi (a hidden or minor error) is an omission in the finer points of tajweed, such as ikhfa, idgham, and ghunnah. It generally does not invalidate salah, but it reduces the beauty and perfection of the recitation.

sorular.soru: How is the recitation level of "Tahqiq" defined?
secenekler: B) The slowest recitation, in which each letter is pronounced with the utmost care and given its due
C) Recitation at a moderate pace
D) The only valid recitation for salah
sorular.aciklama: Tahqiq is the slowest recitation, in which each letter is given its due; it is suitable for the learning stage.

sorular.soru: What is the fastest permissible level of Qur'an recitation?
sorular.aciklama: Hadr is the fastest level of recitation performed while observing the rules of tajweed. It is the fastest of the three levels (tahqiq, tadwir, and hadr).
